newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Russian U.N. envoy against U.K. resolution on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Russian U.N. envoy against U.K. resolution on Iraq.

text.p: Russian ambassador to the United Nations Sergey Lavrov said his country was opposed to the latest U.K. draft resolution on the recent military crisis in Iraq.
Lavrov, speaking to Reuters Thursday, said Russia was maintaining its opposition to the U.K. draft, even as changes were made to the version circulated late Wednesday.
"It would have to be re-drafted (for Russia to approve)," Lavrov said.
Earlier Thursday, Moscow said it would veto the British draft resolution condemning Iraq for its offensive military actions in the north of Iraq last week.

"What is the point of the resolution?," Lavrov said, noting the U.S. said on Wednesday it had accomplished its mission through two days of air strikes in retaliation for Baghdad's taking of the Kurdish city of Arbil.
Further, Lavrov said reports indicate Iraq had withdrawn its forces from Arbil, reducing the intensity of the crisis.
He noted there was no linkage between the issue of Iraq's military moves in the north and the implementation for the oil-for-food accord, Resolution 986.
Lavrov said the humanitarian oil-for-aid plan should be finalized "when the secretary-general decides it is safe."

Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali declared over the weekend that the conditions on the ground in Iraq were not safe, delaying placement of key monitoring personnel necessary to enforce the oil accord and to allow for the sale of Iraqi oil.
Lavrov said there would be no reason for any attempt to delay implementation of the oil-for-food scheme.
When asked if he believed the United States would work to scuttle the plan, Lavrov said, "I don't see how they can technically block the resolution."

Under the oil-for-food plan Iraq is permitted to sell $2 billion worth of crude over a six month period -- on a renewable basis -- to buy food and aid for civilians suffering under sanctions imposed when Baghdad invaded Kuwait in 1990.
The U.N. Security Council is scheduled to meet at 1600 EDT/2000 GMT on the draft resolution for Iraq.
